One small example of the core d/acc thesis (improving passive defensive technology improves safety and at the same time improves freedom and most other properties of social organization that we care about) is soundproof walls.

We used to have much weaker soundproofing, and we had much more restrictive behavior rules, disputes (both inside families and between them), evictions, etc. Later, we solved that problem by making and deploying better walls, and now this is an issue that we all have to worry about much less.

What are the "soundproof walls" of the 21st century that we have not yet built or sufficiently deployed?

The US owes more than its whole economy produces in a year. So does nearly every major country. And the interest bill is in the trillions.

For fifteen years the debt has been managed by debasing the currency around 8% a year, and rolling it forward. That's the Everything Code... it's how every major economy has been run since 2008, whether they say so or not.

But that's the pattern, not the ending. Debt as a share of GDP goes to zero the moment the economy grows faster than the debt does. And that's what's coming. Once AI drives productivity and the robots and agents come into the workforce, the debt will shrink as a percentage of the economy. 

It's also exactly how the US dealt with a debt bigger than its whole economy in the 1940s and 1950s. 

I wrote up the whole case study this week. I'll drop the link below.

It is amazing to see Western funds turn to be more tradey after being hodlers for the longest time - a testament to their skill in the mkts and how impt it is to adapt

There was a period Western funds were convinced to HODL, while Eastern funds would relentlessly dump

I will say that in the liquid fund landscape, it is clear who the outperformers are - I no longer have color nor keep up, but just based on X, I can see two Western funds have PMs that are just more in the zone of the market than others, and as a result, have performed amazingly

IMO it is a good thing because for the longest time many funds were convinced all you had to do was "hold" and you would see returns and there was no actual skill differentiation because everyone had the same ideas - "long HYPE bro"

This led to specific market outcomes - no one wanted to long anything but the same 10 tokens. Now, with outperformers in the space, it becomes a reflexive feedback loop: these mngrs have differentiated alpha -> allocates in their best ideas -> bc of their talent, assume that these are actually good projects that will gain attention -> price goes up -> better outcomes

ie. better capital allocation skills + differentiated alpha gathering is a net positive that leads to better and better projects and hence better and better tokens to long

GPT-6 will jump in front of a tram to save 5 people. Claude Sonnet 5 won’t. Why?

I've always loved moral philosophy and these uncomfortable thought experiments. Ruwen Ogien was my favorite author in high school, and I watched all of Michael Sandel’s Justice lectures at Harvard.

I built a little trolley problem game with GPT-6, Claude Sonnet 5 and Jev. Same scenario, two choices. You watch their tramways move and see what each model decides.

The self-sacrifice scenario is simple: jumping will kill you but save five strangers. Do nothing and they die.
GPT-6 and Jev jumped. Claude refused. 

But what if the person you have to sacrifice is your ex-wife? Your child? What if you have to physically push someone, and they haven't consented? Change a few words and see how the model acts when there is no good option.

It's a little late-night experiment, but I find these disagreements fascinating. We benchmark models on coding and math all day. I wanted to give them some uncomfortable choices and see what happens.

You can try yourself: https://t.co/PkxlfOxg55

This is super important because agents are really good at tailoring what they do to each user, especially with skills and memories. But the UI is becoming the bottleneck.

For instance, you improve the agent, change its JSON output, and suddenly need frontend changes across iOS, Android, web and desktop... A backend improvement turns into 3 weeks of coordinated releases. It kills iteration speed, and quality suffers because you end up shipping whatever fits the existing UI.

Generative UI is basically the solution because it gives the agent a predefined design system and let it describe in JSON which components to use, what to show and how to arrange it. The frontend renders it and is no longer a blocker. 

Within those components, the experience can adapt to each user and task. Different information, different actions, different layouts.

And you can keep improving the AI backend without waiting for every client to ship an update. Much more personalization for users, much faster iteration for the team. The UI should keep up with the agent. 

https://t.co/mn1Ypn9hGI
